clue.text: Right to avoid second drink

indicators.note: to avoid tells us the letter for right keeps out of the word, so it is dropped

parts.note: the latter is the second of two things mentioned

explanation.surface: Someone declines a second drink, saying they have every right to refuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to avoid' removes R (right) from LATTER, leaving the coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: A latte is a milky coffee, a popular drink in cafés.

clue.text: One easily fooled Charles, say

definitions.meaning: a gentle, innocent person easily led

explanation.surface: Charles is a gullible sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamb is used of a meek, gullible person, and is the surname of essayist Charles Lamb.

clue.text: Sadly no stardust at opening of nightspot — move uneasily

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled
at opening of picks the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: No glamour at a nightclub's launch, so people fidget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sadly' rearranges NO STARDUST; 'opening of' adds the N of nightspot.
explanation.definitionFit: To toss and turn is to shift restlessly in bed, unable to sleep.

clue.text: In Harlem I greet guy leaving native country

indicators.note: In indicates the answer is contained inside the next words

explanation.surface: In Harlem someone welcomes a man who has left his homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer hides in 'harlEM I GREEt'.
explanation.definitionFit: An émigré is a person who has left their own country, often for political reasons.

clue.text: One making effort to accommodate me alongside street for period

indicators.note: to accommodate means the outer word takes in and houses the other letters

parts.note: a trier is someone who tries hard

indicators.note: alongside places the two short pieces next to each other

explanation.surface: Someone trying hard makes room for the speaker on a street for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One making effort' is a noun phrase for a person who tries; 'to accommodate' makes it the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A trimester is a term of about three months, such as a stage of pregnancy or an academic term.

clue.text: Ditch worker, incisive

parts.note: a trench is a ditch
an ant is the classic worker in crosswords

explanation.surface: A labourer digging ditches is sharp-minded.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenchant means cutting and sharp, like an incisive remark.

clue.text: Playwright at home occupied by problem with animals

indicators.note: occupied by means the first word has the second living inside it

parts.note: in means at home
BSE (mad cow disease) is a cattle disease

explanation.surface: A dramatist at home is beset by trouble with his animals.
explanation.walkthrough: BSE is bovine spongiform encephalopathy, 'mad cow disease', which hit British cattle in the 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen was the Norwegian dramatist who wrote A Doll's House.

clue.text: One reviewing dismissal looking up underground worker

indicators.note: looking up in a down clue means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: the axe means a dismissal from a job
a miner works underground

explanation.surface: Someone reviewing a sacking finds things improving for a mine worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looking up' reverses AXE to EXA, in a down clue read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An examiner is a person who inspects or assesses, i.e. reviews.

clue.text: Cheers daughter a small bit

parts.note: ta and cheers are both informal British ways to say thanks

explanation.surface: A toast by a daughter is only small.
explanation.definitionFit: A tad is a little: a tiny amount.

clue.text: Representative group replacing Democrat with Republican name

indicators.note: replacing tells us to swap one letter out for another

parts.note: a deputation is a group sent to represent others

explanation.surface: US politics: a delegation switches party allegiance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacing' swaps the D in DEPUTATION for R.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's good name is their reputation, as in 'clear one's name'.

clue.text: One's seen after church ceremony, large-scale

indicators.note: seen after places the second piece after the first in the answer

parts.note: Mass is the Catholic church service
one's, read as 'one has', is I've

explanation.surface: Someone is spotted coming out after a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' must be read as 'one has', i.e. I'VE, not as a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Massive means huge, operating on a very large scale.

clue.text: Like some comedians, Laurel, say, at party

parts.note: Stan Laurel, of Laurel and Hardy, is an example of a Stan
the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A comic like Stan Laurel turns up at a party to perform.
explanation.walkthrough: The DUP is Northern Ireland's Democratic Unionist Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Stand-up comedians perform solo routines standing before a live audience.

clue.text: Kenyan, maybe, furious after losing new flower

indicators.note: after places the trimmed word after the first piece

parts.note: a Kenyan is an example of an African

indicators.note: losing means the letter for new is shed from the word

parts.note: furious can mean violent

explanation.surface: A Kenyan is enraged after losing something new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' drops N (new) from the synonym for furious; 'Kenyan, maybe' flags an example rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: The African violet is a popular small houseplant with purple blooms.

clue.text: Elect editor? Unusual — fairy tale, I suspect

indicators.note: unusual suggests the letters are arranged in an uncommon order

explanation.surface: Choosing an editor would be odd; it sounds like a made-up story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' rearranges ELECT EDITOR. The definition is playful: a machine that would say 'fairy tale, I suspect' of a lie.
explanation.definitionFit: A lie detector, or polygraph, judges whether a statement is a falsehood.

clue.text: Happened to see new partner's ID

indicators.note: new means the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: It turned out someone had to check a fresh partner's identity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges PARTNERS ID.
explanation.definitionFit: Transpired is used loosely to mean took place or occurred.

clue.text: In speech, regretted being impolite

indicators.note: In speech says the word is heard rather than read, so we want its sound-alike

parts.note: rued means regretted

explanation.surface: Someone regretted being impolite in a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: RUED and RUDE are pronounced the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Rude is a direct synonym of impolite: bad-mannered.

clue.text: Strange taste, sure — avoiding ornamentation to the utmost

indicators.note: strange signals that the letters are put into an odd, unfamiliar order

explanation.surface: Someone is sure a flavour is odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' rearranges TASTE SURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere means plain and unadorned; the superlative form means the most severely plain.

clue.text: Child following team? That's of minor interest

indicators.note: following places this piece after the other in the answer

parts.note: a side is a team
issue means offspring, children

explanation.surface: A child who supports a team is of little concern.
explanation.definitionFit: A side issue is a secondary matter, peripheral to the main question.

clue.text: Supply mild case numbers

indicators.note: read as supple-y, i.e. supplely, so the letters bend into a new order

explanation.surface: Provide a gentle instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' is read as the adverb from supple (flexibly), rearranging MILD CASE.
explanation.definitionFit: Decimals are numbers written in base ten with a decimal point.

clue.text: Disgusted as Dean on return pinches University seat

indicators.note: pinches means grabs and holds, so the reversed name encloses the other letters
on return means the name is read backwards

parts.note: taken as the word itself
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Dean, coming back, is revolted to find a university seat has been stolen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is only a link; 'on return' gives NAED, which 'pinches' the other letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Nauseated means sickened, feeling revulsion: the same as disgusted.

clue.text: Ban love token? That's too much!

indicators.note: That's too much says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An exclamation at a romantic gift that seems excessive.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside 'loVE TOken'.
explanation.definitionFit: A veto is a formal prohibition, an order forbidding something.

clue.text: Morning service — parent's collecting money

indicators.note: collecting means gathering up the other word inside

parts.note: ma is a parent, so ma's
tin is slang for money

explanation.surface: A parent takes the church collection at the morning service.
explanation.walkthrough: Tin is old British slang for money; 'collecting' makes the parent's word the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Matins is the morning prayer service in the Anglican church.

clue.text: Procurator's input so tragic, exercise not finished

indicators.note: tragic suggests something ruined, so the letters are wrecked into a new order
not finished means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: Pilates is a form of exercise

explanation.surface: A procurator's contribution was so sad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tragic' rearranges INPUT SO; 'not finished' drops the last S of PILATES.
explanation.definitionFit: Pontius Pilate was the Roman procurator (governor) of Judaea at the time of Jesus's trial.

clue.text: City suite in-law visited regularly

indicators.note: visited regularly means call at every other letter

explanation.surface: An in-law frequently stayed at a city hotel suite.
explanation.definitionFit: Siena is a city in Tuscany, Italy.

clue.text: Tobacco pound

definitions.meaning: a lump of tobacco for chewing
British slang for a pound sterling

explanation.surface: The cost of tobacco.
explanation.definitionFit: Quid is both a chewing wad and British slang for a pound.

clue.text: In pub some may be seen referring to a couple of French articles

definitions.text: In pub some may be seen

parts.note: re means concerning or referring to
la and le are the French feminine and masculine words for 'the'

explanation.surface: A remark about two pieces of French writing.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a whole phrase: something you might see in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Real ale is traditional cask-conditioned beer, sold at British pubs.

clue.text: Respect a partnership

parts.note: we means a pair of people together

explanation.definitionFit: Awe is deep reverence mixed with wonder.

clue.text: Initially somewhat hesitant in Asia, they sign up for massage

indicators.note: Initially tells us to take the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: People in Asia, at first a little unsure, enrol for a massage.
explanation.definitionFit: Shiatsu is a Japanese therapy using finger pressure on points of the body.

clue.text: Rate of movement back and forth in place far away?

indicators.note: back means the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: speed is a rate of movement
going forth, the rate of movement is now pace, read forwards

explanation.surface: A rate of moving to and fro.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rate of movement' gives two synonyms: SPEED read 'back' (DEEPS) and PACE read 'forth'.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep space is the far region of the universe beyond the solar system, a very remote place.

clue.text: Violin shown in board game recalled

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: darts is played on a dartboard

explanation.surface: A violin features in a board game being remembered.
explanation.definitionFit: A Strad is a Stradivarius, a violin made by Antonio Stradivari.
